result.target_topic: Risks related to DGX Cloud and standalone software offerings
result.target_summary: The timing and availability of DGX Cloud services may change, impacting revenue and expenses; these services and standalone software solutions like NVIDIA AI Enterprise may not be successful or generate significant revenue despite significant costs.

Both note that these initiatives may not be successful, will take significant time and resources, and may not generate meaningful revenue.

materiality_analysis.reason: The disclosure change is primarily clarifying. The 2025 text removes 'beginning' to reflect current operational status but retains the core risk that DGX Cloud and software solutions may fail or incur costs without revenue. The specific product examples (AI Enterprise, Omniverse) are listed in both years. No new strategic pivot or material risk escalation is evident.

comparisons.peer_summary: Nvidia's dominance in the Data Center GPU market, its proprietary software ecosystem, and aggressive practices like allocation strategies and product bundling may limit customers' ability to choose non-Nvidia products, limiting AMD's market share and decreasing its margins and profitability.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose risks related to the success and commercial viability of their expanding software and cloud service offerings, though NVIDIA frames it as internal execution/timing risk while AMD frames it as external competitive displacement. NVIDIA warns that its DGX Cloud services 'may not be successful' and that 'timing and availability... has changed,' highlighting internal dependency on new revenue streams. In contrast, AMD highlights how 'Nvidia's dominance... and proprietary software ecosystem' and 'aggressive business practices' may 'limit our ability to compete effectively,' meaning AMD's risk is that a peer's software strategy captures market share, whereas NVIDIA's risk is that its own strategy fails to generate returns. Both identify proprietary software ecosystems as central to competitive strategy and revenue generation.

sentences.text: The timing and availability of these cloud services has changed and may continue to change, impacting our revenue, expenses, and development timelines.
NVIDIA DGX Cloud services may not be successful and will take time, resources, and investment.
We may incur significant costs and may not achieve any significant revenue from these offerings.
Nvidia's dominance in the graphics processing unit market and its aggressive business practices may limit our ability to compete effectively on a level playing field.

Nvidia's Data Center GPU market share position, significant financial resources, introduction of competitive new products and proprietary software ecosystem have enabled it to market and price its products in a manner to encourage the selection of Nvidia-based systems and to influence customers who do business with us.
We expect Nvidia to continue to heavily invest substantial resources in research and development, marketing and other technology companies.

comparisons.peer_topic: Software business growth and cloud competition risks
comparisons.peer_summary: The growth of the software business depends on demand for data center virtualization and hybrid-cloud products; if customers shift compute workloads to public cloud providers or fail to perceive benefits in on-premises solutions, demand may be significantly less than anticipated, adversely affecting business and financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify cloud computing shifts and the timing of software revenue as key risks to their business performance, but with different focal points: NVIDIA focuses on the risk that its own new DGX Cloud services and software may not be successful or timely, while Broadcom focuses on the risk that customer migration to public cloud providers will reduce demand for their on-premises software and semiconductor products. NVIDIA states 'The timing and availability of these cloud services has changed... impacting our revenue,' indicating internal product delivery uncertainty. Broadcom states 'If businesses build new or shift existing compute workloads off-premises to public cloud providers, this could limit the market for on-premises deployments,' indicating external demand substitution risk. Both link cloud trends directly to revenue uncertainty and business strategy viability.

sentences.text: The timing and availability of these cloud services has changed and may continue to change, impacting our revenue, expenses, and development timelines.
NVIDIA DGX Cloud services may not be successful and will take time, resources, and investment.
We also offer or plan to offer standalone software solutions, including NVIDIA AI Enterprise, NVIDIA Omniverse, NVIDIA DRIVE, and several other software solutions.
The growth of our software business depends on demand for our data center virtualization products, as well as customer acceptance of our products, services and business strategy.
Current and future customers may not perceive benefits associated with adopting our hybrid-cloud and enterprise-grade private cloud platform or our simplified product portfolios.

If demand is significantly less than anticipated or we fail to realize the expected returns on our business strategy, our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows may be adversely affected.

comparisons.peer_summary: Cloud service providers are developing their own semiconductors and abstracting hardware through software, making it difficult to differentiate Intel's products and potentially reducing demand for Intel chips.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose risks arising from the shift of data center workloads to the cloud and the resulting challenges in differentiation and customer dependency, but from opposite positions in the value chain: NVIDIA faces risk from the uncertainty of its own cloud service offerings, while Intel faces risk from cloud providers developing their own chips and abstracting hardware, which reduces demand for Intel's products. NVIDIA states 'NVIDIA DGX Cloud services may not be successful and will take time, resources, and investment,' highlighting execution risk in a new cloud layer. Intel states 'Some cloud service provider customers have also internally developed... their own semiconductors... [and] abstract hardware under layers of software, which can make it more difficult to differentiate our products,' highlighting strategic risk from customer vertical integration. Both recognize cloud computing as a transformative force altering traditional hardware/software sales models.

sentences.text: The timing and availability of these cloud services has changed and may continue to change, impacting our revenue, expenses, and development timelines.
NVIDIA DGX Cloud services may not be successful and will take time, resources, and investment.
We may incur significant costs and may not achieve any significant revenue from these offerings.
Some cloud service provider customers have also internally developed, and may continue to develop, their own semiconductors, including designs customized for their specific computing workloads.

In addition, cloud services can be marketed to end users based on service levels or features rather than hardware specifications, or they can abstract hardware under layers of software, which can make it more difficult to differentiate our products to customers and end users.

The shift of data center workloads to the cloud has also adversely affected, and may continue to affect, sales to enterprise customers when end users have elected to migrate workloads from their own internal data center infrastructures to cloud service providers.
